claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Finite binary semi-directed, LSA-rootable, outer-labeled planar, galled networks on n>=4 labeled taxa, with the pinned parallel-edge/bigon conventions and arbitrary finite level and blob count. A query returns the complete set of distinct displayed resolved quartet topologies on four requested taxa, not multiplicities or gene-tree probabilities; the required output is the full nontrivial displayed-split union and any common circular order. No circle, tree or blob tree is supplied. The lower bound is ceil(log_3((2n-5)!!)). The accepted order learner uses at most (n-3)(11 ceil(log_2 n)+15) calls. For a supplied common circle and k distinct splits, the sparse component uses at most min{binomial(n,4),(n-2)(n-3),2n-6+4k ceil(log_2(n-1))}, without knowing k. The inherited source bound k<=13n-27 gives the matching O(n log n) joint upper bound; caching caps distinct calls by binomial(n,4).

claims.title: Three settings suffice for a probability floor, and four for certainty

plain_language.question: With the network's control structure known, how many fixed settings expose every displayed split or quartet?
plain_language.what_we_learned: The worst-case minima are three settings for the stated positive occurrence floor and four for guaranteed occurrence.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use a sharp topology-focused control budget instead of forcing every routing combination.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not recover all numerical laws, work with unknown control IDs or justify replacing topology-equivalent parts in every biological experiment.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Finite binary semi-directed, LSA-rootable, outer-labeled planar, galled networks on n>=4 labeled taxa, with the pinned parallel-edge/bigon conventions and arbitrary finite level and blob count. Every boundary port is taxon-bearing. Under the stated graph-informed contract, the graph/outer embedding or a certified interaction map is supplied, original hybrid IDs are retained, controls are fixed parameter-oblivious partial parent-forcing assignments, and forcing a parent leaves the other laws unchanged, and natural independent routing probabilities lie in [g,1-g] for 0<g<=1/2. Uniformly over this admitted source class, the worst-case minimum number of environments is three so that every displayed nontrivial split and quartet occurrence has probability at least g in at least one environment, and four so each occurs with certainty in at least one environment; these are not asserted to be the exact minima at every fixed taxon count. The source-admitted lower witnesses and switching-wise <=3-port topology quotient use the pinned source conventions.

claims.title: Five labels suffice to test the whole anchor-parameter domain, and four do not

plain_language.question: How small can the test configurations be when checking which scoring parameters always work?
plain_language.what_we_learned: For the stated anchor-positivity criterion, checking every representation through five distinct labels is enough for all finite sizes; stopping at four misses a real obstruction.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Replace an unbounded parameter test with the proved sharp finite collection.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: Five labels is not five quartet queries, a five-label restriction of every configuration, or a universal biological sample-size claim.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For every real four-score vector (c,s,a,o), with the exceptional anchor-sharing entry fixed at 1, universal nonnegativity of every circular anchor coefficient on finite adjacent singleton/doubleton plane-tree representations with n>=3 distinct taxon labels is equivalent to checking all such coefficients with at most five total labels, and to s=o=1, 1/2<=a<=1, 0<=c<=a. Five is the least sufficient cutoff: an actual five-label representation has a negative coefficient at (1,1,1/2,1), while all three/four-label tests pass. Labels include duplicated taxa. The proof retains the six-label structural reduction and uses equality of the five/six-label normalized inequality collections; it does not assert that each six-label configuration restricts to five while preserving its coefficient.

claims.title: Rounding tolerates errors below one half, and the uniform limit is sharp

plain_language.question: How much error can the original distance matrix tolerate while still permitting exact recovery?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Entrywise error strictly below one half allows exact matrix recovery by rounding; with a correct circular order, it also recovers the split support. The uniform threshold cannot be enlarged.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use a sharp deterministic robustness guarantee when the stated raw-matrix error promise is justified.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not supply a statistical estimator, a number of gene samples, an order-finding algorithm or a guarantee for arbitrarily rescaled distances.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For every finite binary semi-directed LSA-rootable outer-labeled planar galled network on at least four taxa in the pinned source class, the original unnormalized NANUQ distance has integer entries. If an observed matrix has entrywise sup-norm error strictly below 1/2, nearest-integer rounding recovers the exact full raw matrix without needing an order. Given a correct common circular order, the accepted exact-support theorem then recovers the displayed-split union. An admitted four-taxon tree/cycle pair has raw matrices at sup-norm distance 1 and different supports; their common midpoint defeats every decoder at closed error radius 1/2 and every larger strict radius, even with the correct order supplied. This is a sharp uniform result over the class, not a separate sharpness claim for every fixed larger taxon count.

origin.detail: A deterministic robustness and sharpness continuation of the all-level original-NANUQ theorem.

claims.programme: Soft Sciences · identification, measurement and evidence
claims.title: Extra observations can resolve ambiguity, but their assumptions matter

plain_language.question: Which additional observations actually distinguish competing explanations?
plain_language.what_we_learned: A sum alone hides its components, a specified second probe recovers them, and known bias bounds translate into exact uncertainty intervals. Correct discriminating labels remove rivals; incorrect exact labels can remove the truth.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Inspect precisely what extra measurement or evidence justifies a conclusion before fitting or interpreting a model.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: These noiseless integer and exact-label results do not establish an empirical bias bound, a sample-complexity guarantee or robustness to noisy labels.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: The 27 declarations are nine each in Identifiability, Measurement and Learning. For theta in Int x Int, observing only its sum is noninjective, while observing the sum and first component is injective. For arbitrary prediction functions, more probes preserve identification and postprocessing preserves observation equivalence. In the integer response model response(a,bias)=a+bias, a supplied differential-bias interval [-delta,delta] implies latent difference in [observed gap-delta,observed gap+delta]; an upper bias bound below the observed gap fixes the latent ordering. For deterministic hypotheses and finite exact-label lists, adding correct discriminating evidence preserves a fitting truth and excludes a disagreeing rival; a wrong label excludes truth, inconsistent labels admit no fit, and duplicate identical constraints leave the fitting set unchanged.

The integer examples do not resolve those sources' broader scientific agendas.

claims.title: Identical observations can conceal different intervention effects

plain_language.question: Can two explanations agree on every allowed observation and still disagree about what an intervention does?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes. Two explicit Boolean models have identical observational records but different responses when treatment is set independently.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Show exactly why the permitted observational input alone cannot support a universally correct effect estimator.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This elementary collision is not a general causal-discovery algorithm or a resolution of the richer homophily-versus-contagion problem.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Six declarations concern BinaryModel outcome functions on Boolean treatment and background. The treatment-copy model Y=T and common-cause model Y=U give identical observed functions u -> (u,Y(u,u)) when T=U, but disagree at the intervention T=true,U=false. Their effectNumerator values are 2 and 0. Hence there is no estimator from the complete permitted observational function to Int that returns effectNumerator correctly for every BinaryModel. Equality of all treatment/background response values identifies the full model function. Interpreting the numerator as twice an average treatment effect additionally assumes uniform Boolean background.
claims.prior_work: Observational non-identification is classical. Shalizi and Thomas (2011) supply a richer network-motivating predecessor, not an equivalent theorem proved by this Boolean example.
claims.our_contribution: The original package gives a transparent checked collision and universal-estimator impossibility consequence in the declared finite model, with the observation/effect distinction explicit. This is formalization of an established principle, not a newly solved causal-inference open problem.

claims.programme: Soft Sciences · contact structure, incentives and allocation
claims.title: Connectedness, trust and an acceptable deal are different requirements

plain_language.question: Does a connected society automatically have trust and incentives to cooperate?
plain_language.what_we_learned: No such implication follows from the model. Very sparse direct contacts allow unbounded reach, while cooperation and participation obey separate exact payoff and budget conditions.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Keep structural reach, group membership, trust and incentive compatibility separate when making an argument.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: The model does not show that labels never affect people, that institutions can finance sanctions, or that a political intervention works.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: The 26 declarations comprise the original 16 Solidarity and 10 CollectiveAction declarations. On Nat with successor/predecessor adjacency, every pair is connected, reach from zero is unbounded, and every neighbor of a belongs to {a+1,a-1}; the last theorem is containment, not a separate formal degree-cardinality statement. Overlapping membership and a separately defined empty trust relation are explicit examples. In the integer one-shot payoff (benefit if the other contributes) minus (cost if one contributes, sanction otherwise), mutual contribution is weakly stable against unilateral withdrawal iff cost<=sanction. For fixed uncongested task capabilities and participation reward>=cost with zero outside option, total surplus need not make an offered allocation acceptable. With unrestricted integer transfers, there exists an acceptable two-person share iff costA+costB<=budget; acceptable shares are exactly [costA,budget-costB].
claims.prior_work: Elementary graph connectivity, set inclusion, unilateral payoff comparisons and transfer feasibility are established mathematics. The source's broader social interpretation and formal-social-choice bibliography are motivation, not empirical implications or claims to supersede prior formalization.

claims.title: Every start and phase has an exact matching answer

plain_language.question: How long can a prescribed Thue–Morse pattern be followed from any starting point?
plain_language.what_we_learned: There is an exact all-start formula and digit evaluator, plus an attained maximum for every phase and an exact classification of sharp cases.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Compute the actual longest match and distinguish ordinary starts from exceptional long matches without scanning every path.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This is a target-dependent graph result, not every possible pattern search, arithmetic-progression statistic or biological measurement.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For digit-parity Thue–Morse t, the graph has edges w−1→w labelled t(w) and w−2→w labelled 1−t(w), for w≥2, and no edge 0→1. A path's kth edge must read t(k). The attained maximum L(v) has a complete closed form for all natural v, with L(0)=1. For v≥1, 3L(v)≤8v−1, with equality exactly at v=3·2^n−1, where L=8·2^n−3. The proved ten-coordinate integer digit recurrence evaluates this maximum. For the own-target graph of s_a(k)=t(k+a), shifting both target and graph, an actual maximum exists at every natural a,v. For v≥1, 3L_a(v)≤8v+5a−1, with equality iff some n≥0 has a≤2^n and v=3·2^n−a−1; then L_a(v)=8·2^n−a−3. Named endpoints are FullHeight.height_isMaximum/height_closed_form, DigitRecurrence.evaluate_isMaximum, PhaseHeight.height_isMaximum and PhaseExtremal.shifted_extremal_iff.

claims.title: Finite prefix changes have an exactly computable global cost

plain_language.question: If the beginning of the target pattern changes, can its worst global matching penalty still be found exactly?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes. An explicit finite search finds the smallest additive allowance that works at every positive start, and a start inside the search attains it.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Certify the exact robustness cost for one specified finite prefix edit, not just use a universal overestimate.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: The theorem does not give a fast practical search or cover arbitrary edits indefinitely far along the sequence.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Let m≥0 and let a binary target s agree with digit-parity Thue–Morse at every index k≥m, with no restrictions on its first m bits. Let L_s(v) be the attained maximum matching length in the original own-target BinaryAvoidance graph. Set N(m)=3·2^(m+3)+m and B_s=max_{1≤v≤N(m)}(3L_s(v)−8v), in the integers. Every positive v satisfies 3L_s(v)≤8v+B_s, some positive v≤N(m) attains equality, and an integer B is valid at every positive start iff B_s≤B. Also −1≤B_s≤8m−1. FiniteEditExact.height computes the needed maximum; FiniteEditOptimum.individual_optimum_attained and individual_additive_constant_iff supply the global finite-reduction endpoint.

claims.title: Huge finite matches need not become an infinite match

plain_language.question: Does matching longer and longer finite patterns imply that some infinite match exists?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Not in this model. A specified word's period-break data bounds its matches, yet suitable aperiodic targets have finite matches exceeding any supplied growth schedule while admitting no infinite match.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Separate a genuine infinite-realization claim from very large finite evidence, and obtain explicit bounds when a period-break modulus is supplied.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: There is no one target asserted to beat every growth function, nor a word-independent bound for all aperiodic targets.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: In the manuscript's own-target graph P_s, a modulus M(v,b) supplies, for each offset d≤v, an index i in [b,M(v,b)) at which s(i) differs from the label required for a constant-offset two-step edge. Equivalently, even d=2e breaks antiperiod e+1 and odd d=2e+1 breaks period e+1. With B_0=0 and B_{r+1}=M(v,B_r), every actual matching prefix from v has length ell<B_{v+1}. If M(v,b)≤b+R, then ell<(v+1)R. Every non-eventually-periodic target has such a modulus, with existence using choice. Conversely, for every f:Nat→Nat there exists a non-eventually-periodic target s, with no infinite matching path in P_s, and strictly increasing starts v_j having finite matching prefixes longer than f(v_j). The target may depend on f. Named audited endpoints include QuantitativeModulus.prefix_length_lt_clock, prefix_length_lt_uniform_windows and SlowAvoidance.arbitrarily_slow_avoidance.
claims.prior_work: The own-target avoidance construction belongs to the September classification programme; its eventually-periodic positive direction credits Alexander. claims.title: Typical-scale totals differ sharply from exceptional long matches

plain_language.question: What happens when we total matching lengths across all starts rather than choose the most extreme one?
plain_language.what_we_learned: An exact formula gives the total below every power of two, and a digit algorithm computes the total below any cutoff. The mean grows logarithmically even though selected starts have linear height.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Calculate exact aggregate behavior at large cutoffs without enumerating every starting point.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: A mean alone is not a concentration bound, a typical-value theorem or a limiting distribution.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For the actual attained matching height L(v) of CB-SEQ-004, let A_k=sum_{0≤v<2^k} L(v). Then A_0=1, A_1=1, A_2=6, and for k≥3, A_k=29(3k+1)2^k/72−(k+3)−(7/9)(−1)^k. Consequently A_k/2^k is asymptotic to (29/24)k. The inherited ten-coordinate digit representation yields a fixed-size algorithm computing sum_{0≤v<N}L(v) in O(log N) integer-matrix operations for positive N, with zero cutoff handled directly. The hand proof includes a finite matrix-annihilator identity and exact base cases; it is not extrapolation from numerical totals.

claims.title: A precise coding transfers patterns without preserving every property

plain_language.question: What survives when a binary pattern is turned into a juggling schedule?
plain_language.what_we_learned: An explicit coding preserves constrained matching lengths exactly, while equal versus unequal block lengths determine whether the prescribed-prefix generating function is rational.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use a fully specified encoding to transfer a theorem and understand why restricting a freely concatenable system changes its counting law.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This is not a new unrestricted juggling-height bound, an unrestricted counting theorem, or a practical compression result.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: At the three-ball ground state, encode 0 by primitive block (3) and 1 by (4,2). Expand each original matching-graph edge into its own code path, retaining original vertices and distinct internal vertices. Starting only at an original v, the attained constrained throw-match height is H(v)=W(L(v)), where W(2m)=3m and W(2m+1)=3m+1+t(m). For v≥1, H(v)≤4v with equality exactly v=3·2^(2r)−1. Separately, choose two distinct primitive loops at one fixed b-ball state, with positive beat lengths a,c, and count exactly one word for each Thue–Morse block-prefix length, including the empty prefix. Its series F_{a,c}(z) equals [1+(z^a+z^c)/2]/(1−z^(a+c))+(z^a−z^c)P(z^(a+c))/2, where P(x)=product_{r≥0}(1−x^(2^r)). If a=c then F=1/(1−z^a); if a≠c the unit circle is a natural boundary. For b≥2, F(b^(−s))−1 has boundary Re(s)=0.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For n≥1 let u_n be the fixed point starting 0 of tau_n:0→0^n1^n,1→1^n0^n. plain_language.question: Can one positive Collatz start follow a fixed Thue–Morse arrangement of valuation blocks forever?

Let t be ordinary binary Thue–Morse starting 0 and let B_0,B_1 be any fixed nonempty finite words of positive integer valuations. If B_{t_0}B_{t_1}… is the exact valuation sequence of one positive odd N, then U^j(N)=N for some j>0. No equal-codeword-length or average-valuation hypothesis is assumed. claims.title: Recurring reproductive links determine an ancestry property under explicit mixing

plain_language.question: When do recurring links between reproductive communities determine long-run ancestry?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Under strong local mixing and no lineage extinction, an infinite group has the identical-ancestors property (IAP) exactly when all but finitely many members lie in one recurrent strongly connected component.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Classify the stated ancestry property and construct connected, ancestry-convex component tails without confusing recurring contact with a measured species boundary.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: The mixing premise is substantial and is not almost surely satisfied by ordinary finite Wright–Fisher reproduction. This does not identify empirical species or maximal clusters.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: A finite nonempty deme set, organisms indexed by natural numbers with a separate generation map, finite generation prefixes, occupied cohorts in every deme, one-generation parent edges, same-deme parent coverage, and one uniform positive finite lag giving complete within-deme dissemination from every organism are assumed. Ancestry means a nonempty parent path. The identical-ancestors property (IAP, the source's identical-ancestor-point axiom) says that each member of a set has either finitely many descendants or finitely many non-descendants within that set. For every infinite subset, IAP holds iff it is contained modulo finitely many members in one recurrent strongly connected component; that component is unique. Sparse subsets are allowed: this is not equality with the whole component. Whole-history IAP is equivalent to recurrent strong connectivity. A common-cutoff component tail is infinite, connected, ancestrally convex and reflecting. Concrete one-way and bidirectional examples and uniqueness are included.
claims.prior_work: Alexander's strict-ancestry and specieslike-cluster predicates, structured-pedigree ancestry mixing, and temporal recurrence/reachability are antecedents. claims.title: One shared random process joins a marker barrier to almost-sure ancestry mixing
claims.programme: Feedback models · same-draw marker and parent process

plain_language.question: Can a positive marker-barrier statistic coexist with the identical-ancestors property in the very same population process?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes, for the explicitly constructed process. The same random draws produce both the marker path and parent graph, whose whole-history identical-ancestors property (IAP) holds almost surely.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Connect the declared marker calculation to an actual ancestry process, instead of choosing an unrelated graph or leaving the infinite-process connection pending.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not equate the statistic with a separately constructed infinite-stream marker-fixation event, cover other genetic regimes or establish an empirical species boundary.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: There are two adults per generation, one per deme, with two parent slots per child and selfing allowed. Four independent uniform Fin14 draws per generation are reused for both parental identity and marker homologue; local parent probability is 6/7, foreign 1/7 and homologue probability 1/2. The pure selected-state induction model has a transition-zero marker pulse followed by ordinary inheritance. The completed bounded R1–R6 theorem proves raw/compressed-record transport, all 81 ordinary and nine pulse marginal identities and off-support closure, a measurable count/parent process, and every finite-path frozen-kernel product law. The designated parent-table mass is 36/2401. For an organism born strictly before the chosen future starting generation and k future generations, non-resolution probability is at most (2365/2401)^k, also conditional on any positive-mass complete earlier raw-history event. Whole-history identical-ancestors property (IAP) holds almost surely: each member has finitely many descendants or finitely many non-descendants within that history. The frozen-kernel RI=3/7, finite-path realization and actual-law IAP are conjoined. Exact avoidance probability and non-resolution bound are not equality of events, and marker counts are not independent across generations.
claims.prior_work: Classical product probability, recurrence of a positive-probability symbol, and extinction-or-spread synchronization are reused. This actual-law proof permits extinction and does not derive its premise from the no-extinction recurrent-component theorem.

claims.title: A finite ancestry graph does not determine its infinite population's specieslike status

plain_language.question: Does a finite genome-ancestry graph determine whether its whole infinite completion is specieslike?
plain_language.what_we_learned: No. Every admitted finite graph has two compatible infinite completions with opposite answers, despite preserving all its old edges and ancestry paths.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Identify which assumptions about admissible futures are needed before finite ancestry evidence can justify a future-inclusive conclusion.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This is not a universal impossibility theorem for DNA inference or biological species identification.

Abstract topology completions, not extension of future interval annotations, a genome-to-organism owner map, equal DNA probability laws, or a universal species-inference impossibility.

claims.title: Exact laws identify three-taxon relationships, but finite samples do not give certainty

plain_language.question: How can an exact probability law identify a relationship while finite observations remain uncertain?
plain_language.what_we_learned: The exact non-collapsed three-taxon law identifies the relationship. With positive noise, every finite sample fits every label with positive probability; an error smaller than half the probability gap preserves the correct answer.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Keep ideal-law identification, uncertainty from finite data and robustness of estimated probabilities separate.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: The taxa are already designated. This neither discovers species boundaries nor guarantees certainty from finitely many observed genes.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For the prescribed law P(s)=1−2c/3 and P(g≠s)=c/3, 0≤c<1 identifies both the rooted label and c; c=1 collapses the labels. For 0<c≤1 every finite ordered sample has positive product mass under every label, precluding a uniformly certain finite decoder. An estimate with coordinate error ε and 2ε<1−c retains the correct strict maximizer; the half-gap boundary is sharp. The singleton-mass adverse witness has mass at least (c/3)^n, not a formally measured total error lower bound. Three preassigned taxa and a prescribed rooted gene-tree law; no coalescent derivation, raw-DNA decoding, species delimitation or aggregate error measure is formalized. The separate Hoeffding bound min(1,2exp(−n(1−c)^2/2)) is a standard written derivation, not a Lean endpoint.

claims.title: Missing diploid ownership can change long-term ancestry; informative samples are characterized exactly

plain_language.question: What remains undetermined if every realized copy transmission is known but the pairing of copies into organisms is missing?
plain_language.what_we_learned: The same complete copy history can have opposite long-term organism-ancestry properties. In the constructed family, exactly characterized ownership samples resolve that ambiguity.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Specify which individual-association records are essential and distinguish informative infinite records from finite evidence.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: The result is not about every pedigree, noisy DNA observations or identical stochastic likelihoods. The infinite-record decoder is not a terminating decision algorithm.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: One fixed eight-lane infinite transmission graph admits, after every prescribed finite mixing-prefix length, two diploid owner schedules with opposite whole-population IAP/specieslike/inspecies status. IAP means that each member has finitely many descendants or finitely many non-descendants within the population. Both have four founders, four organisms per generation, exactly two copies per organism, two distinct parents per nonfounder and two children per organism, weak connectivity and real generation dates; every organism edge is exactly witnessed by transmission. In this mixing/delayed-splitting family, the noiseless lane-0/lane-3 co-ownership record on a fixed mask identifies IAP iff the sampled odd generations are unbounded. Even complete ownership at every even generation fails. With a supplied even upper bound B≥2 on switch times, identification is equivalent to sampling an odd generation after B, and one query at B+1 suffices. Any prescribed prefix length of this mixing history, not every possible ownership prefix. Same realized history is not equality of stochastic likelihoods. No biological law or positive probability for the entire infinite construction, no generic pedigree decoder, no noisy/adaptive sampling and no inference of owner labels from phasing. Exact image edges need not lift organism paths. Infinite-record decoder is set-theoretic, not a uniformly terminating algorithm.

claims.title: Independent inheritance blocks have an exact recovery probability; matching marginals do not suffice

plain_language.question: When do observed symbol matches recover sampled families, and does collecting more blocks always add information?
plain_language.what_we_learned: The stated independent-block model has an exact recovery probability. Repeated correlated blocks can have every correct one-block marginal yet provide no additional recovery gain.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use a precise finite-observation benchmark and check whether an independence assumption really supports the claimed benefit of more data.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not recover arbitrary pedigrees, prove the full multigeneration REC-GEN theorem, or make ordinary DNA letters unique parent identifiers.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: With disjoint parental pairs, per-block distinct parent symbols, exact observations and independent fair child/block copying, connect children sharing a symbol in any block. For B≥1 and nonempty family sizes m_i, exact partition recovery has probability ∏_i[1−(2^(m_i−1)−1)2^(−B(m_i−1))]. The estimator uses only observed symbols. A correlated law repeating each child's one fair bit across all blocks retains each full one-block marginal but leaves one-family success at 2^(1−m), independently of positive B. Pathwise, adding blocks cannot spoil a correct recovery even without independence. The formal notation uses m_i=n_i+1 and includes singleton families and the empty family collection by the product convention. Not full multigeneration REC-GEN, estimator optimality, ordinary DNA-symbol collision handling, a continuous ARG-to-block-law coupling, or infinite IAP/species inference. The formal observed-output theorem uses a finite measurable alphabet. The repeated-law formal endpoint is one-family. Written pair-event distribution identifiability, union/error bounds and couple-vertex construction have separately stated non-Lean status.

plain_language.question: Does seeing no event prove that it is impossible?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Not in the stated independent-trial model. The unavoidable finite-sample error and the distinct rules attaining its two sharp optima are already derived.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Observe n≥0 independent fully observed binary trials. M0 always returns zero; Me has one known fixed event probability 0<e<1. Randomized decisions are allowed. With q=(1−e)^n, the minimum sum of the two error probabilities is q, the minimum worst error is q/(1+q), and equal-prior Bayes error is q/2. Both respective attaining rules are supplied, including n=0. For fixed e>0 error can approach zero as n grows, but cannot be zero for finite n. Allowing arbitrarily small e prevents a uniform finite-n worst-error guarantee below one half. A supplied e_min>0 bounds the all-zero probability by (1−e_min)^n, supporting a specified error level rather than certainty. The known-rate, independent-trial and complete-observation assumptions are load-bearing.

claims.title: Matching states either continue forever or have an exact finite height

plain_language.question: What exactly separates an infinite pattern-matching continuation from one that must stop?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Classical rank and pruning methods give an exact answer on reachable states. Under finite branching, every state either continues forever or has an attained longest continuation; complete finite duplication preserves the corresponding finite heights.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use an exact source-specific certificate and identify information that matching heights retain or omit, without inventing a new rank theory.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For a labelled graph and fixed infinite word s, use reachable vertex/phase states (v,k) witnessed by a path spelling the first k letters. Avoidance is equivalent to well-foundedness of forward continuation and to a decreasing ordinal certificate, without a finite-branching premise. With finite per-label children, natural certificates suffice; states surviving all finite successor-pruning rounds form exactly the infinite-continuation core and the greatest successor fixed point. Its complement is forward closed and well-founded. Each such mortal state has a pointwise least natural height h, equal to an attained maximum number of further matching edges, survives precisely n≤h and is removed at h+1; other states may realize the word, so global avoidance is not assumed for this dichotomy. A phase-zero state survives iff its start realizes the full target. A separate complete positive finite-fibre blow-up preserves and reflects reachable phases and every finite continuation length, and transports least attained natural heights through the actual projection. Its avoiding-population endpoint derives the needed hypotheses. This complete blow-up is not terminal cloning and need not preserve exact parent counts. claims.title: Every organism belongs to a maximal cluster under a fixed founder window

plain_language.question: Can a maximal ancestry cluster exist without requiring one common ancestor?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes, under the stated graph and cluster conditions, a fixed real window containing all founder birthdates gives a complete existence theorem through every organism.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Replace a common-ancestor constraint with a precisely defined founding-window condition in this mathematical maximality problem.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Let organism identifiers be Nat, with real birthdates, strictly chronological parent edges, finite strict real birth sublevels and finite children. Tied birthdates are allowed; identifiers need not be chronological and no finite-root premise is required. For a nonempty set S, founders are its members with no strict ancestor in S, not necessarily ambient roots, and m(S) is its attained earliest birthdate. Fix one real duration Δ. The admissible sets are nonempty, induced-undirected connected, ancestrally convex, satisfy IAP and reflection, and have every founder born by m(S)+Δ. IAP means each member has either finitely many descendants or finitely many non-descendants in S; reflection means every member with infinitely many ambient descendants has infinitely many descendants in S. Every admissible set extends to an inclusion-maximal set in this same class with the same Δ. For every Δ≥0 and every original organism v, such a maximal set containing v exists. The proof supplies the actual seed and transports all competitors back to the original graph and literal dates. This is constrained maximality, not maximality among all specieslike sets. The written coeval-two-founder example shows the window need not imply common ancestry; it is not a separately registered Lean endpoint.

claims.title: A continuous recombination model records valid histories and stops almost surely

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: For every finite natural sample count n≥1, real genome length L>0, merger scale a>0 and split scale b≥0, set θ=2b/a and q(k)=bk+a k(k−1)/2 for k≥2. The constructed Ionescu–Tulcea count law jumps up with mass bk/q(k), down with mass a k(k−1)/(2q(k)), and absorbs at one. Independent unit exponentials give pre-stop waits E_i/q(K_i). Wong's literal specialization is a=1, b=ρ; b is a total per-lineage whole-genome rate, not an unstated per-unit-length rate. The actual recorder consumes a uniform active lineage for splitting or uniform unordered pair of distinct active lineage IDs for merging, with normalized-Lebesgue cuts in (0,L). Splits assign full-genome left/right partitions; they are not truncated to sampled ancestral material. The conditional spatial-mark cylinder is proved for the actual recursively selected frontier. The measurable output stores the finite stopping horizon J, explicit success/failure, capped state snapshots and real timestamps, with constant tails after J. Under its law it is almost surely a valid chronological finite marked history with final active count one. The measurable projection reading frontier cardinalities and timestamps from this stored output alone has exactly the constructed count/event-time law; it does not recover time from an undated graph. Proved invariants tie sample IDs, stable lineage identities, interval coverage and event counts to the actual recursion. Event count and physical stopping time are almost surely finite; n=1 has zero events/time, n≥2 has positive physical time, and b=0 is included. No deterministic uniform bound is asserted. The count supplier also proves a finite sum of nonabsorption probabilities, but no expected physical-time endpoint or growth asymptotic is assigned here. Malformed starts, nonhitting paths and invalid consumed transitions fail explicitly; unused mark components and post-stop tails are ignored. Clock positivity is almost sure under the law, not an all-input parser check. ValidDated is a measurable support predicate, not a converse recognizer for all legal intermediate histories. The raw root/single-parent/single-crossover encoding has a classical inverse on its explicit range without distinct parent endpoints. claims.title: Preparation and order of limits change a finite-population marker assay

plain_language.question: Do a finite population, its preparation and the order of limits change what a marker-barrier assay means?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes. Genetic long burn-in eventually removes the selected background in this finite model, while a properly prepared reset regime has an exact all-N barrier formula; two diversity limits disagree.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Two demes have N>=2 diploids each and exchange exactly k uniformly selected individuals each way, 1<=k<N, m=k/N. Soft additive viability has 0<=s<1; independent gamete/offspring draws allow repeated parents and selfing, recombination lies in [0,1/2], and the declared order is exchange, viability, recombinant mating, then epimutation. One direction's k migrants receive the marker after exchange and before selection; B0=m/2 and R=1−E[B_T]/B0 uses unconditional global marker frequency. A positive two-generation accessibility bound gives geometric fixation/loss tails for a nonmutating allele. At fixed finite N and genetic mu=0, selected-background burn-in L→infinity makes the marker barrier tend to zero uniformly over subsequent horizons, including terminal fixation. Complete reset mu=1/2,phi=1 from a locally reset-compatible selected background before the pulse gives R=s(1−m)/(1−ms) for every admitted N,k, recombination and T>=1, including terminal; mirrored initialization or an unmarked reset generation supplies that preparation. This is N-independence at fixed m, not fixed k. At mu=0 from mirrored pure initialization and fixed rational m along compatible k=Nm census sizes, H=2*pbar*(1−pbar) has iterated limits 0 when finite-N long burn-in is first and 1/2 when infinite-census limit is first. H is global allelic diversity, not heterozygote frequency, and no corresponding RI limit interchange theorem is claimed. claims.title: A supplied owner map can preserve ancestry properties under explicit conditions

plain_language.question: When can a supplied map from a rich history to organism owners preserve precise ancestry properties?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Exact ancestry correspondence and finite owner fibres transfer the stated properties under their separate hypotheses. The identical-ancestors property even tolerates finitely many wrong ancestry answers per representative. A merely sound owner map is not enough.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Check the exact assumptions needed before transferring a graph-level ancestry conclusion, and distinguish a valid conditional theorem from a claim that owners can be inferred from genomic data.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not infer ownership, validate a biological model or classify species empirically. The finite-error relaxation transfers only the identical-ancestors property; maximality equivalence is restricted to whole-owner, saturated candidates.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: The identical-ancestors property (IAP) means that each member has finitely many descendants or finitely many nondescendants inside the candidate. It is a mathematical graph predicate, not an empirical species label. Let R and E be supplied directed graphs on Nat, let q:Nat→Nat be a supplied owner map, let S be an organism candidate, and let C=q⁻¹(S) contain all rich representatives of those owners. Ancestry means nonempty directed paths. If q is onto, every owner fibre is finite, and ancestry is equivalent for every pair of representatives with different owners, then IAP and reflection agree between C in R and S in E. No uniform fibre bound is required. Reflection means that each candidate member with infinitely many ambient descendants also has infinitely many descendants within the candidate. The exact ancestry hypothesis is both directions for every such representative pair, not mere soundness, exact image edges or an existential lift. Under path soundness alone, an R ancestry path maps to owner equality or E ancestry, and convexity pulls back. With an onto owner map, soundness also transfers a common ancestor downward; weak connectivity descends when S is convex. With onto ownership, exact different-owner ancestry and acyclic E, convexity is equivalent. Adding finite fibres gives descent of the source-defined specieslike predicate, namely nonempty induced-undirected connectivity plus IAP plus ancestral convexity. Adding internal weak connectivity of every owner fibre gives specieslike equivalence on saturated candidates C. Under those stronger premises, target maximality is equivalent to rich maximality among all saturated inverse-image candidates. Unrestricted rich maximality of a saturated C also descends. The reverse implication to unrestricted rich maximality is not asserted. Neither the full biosphere/date/child-count conditions nor the fixed founder-window property is automatically transported. The later finite-error extension proves IAP(R,C) iff IAP(E,S) assuming only onto q, finite fibres and, for each a∈C, finitely many b∈C whose R-ancestry answer differs from E-ancestry(q(a),q(b)). The finite error set and its size may vary with a; no common bound is needed. Errors between different owners are permitted and no agreement outside C is required. This IAP theorem needs neither acyclicity, soundness nor connected fibres. It does not transfer reflection, convexity, connectivity, maximality or specieslike status under those relaxed premises. “Finite errors” refers to transitive ancestry answers, not finitely many edited immediate-parent edges. A proved countercontrol fixes one infinite connected rich fork history and identity ownership. Both the fork pedigree and a chain pedigree are sound interpretations, with onto singleton fibres and the stated natural/real-date biosphere properties; the chain is whole-population specieslike and the fork fails IAP. It shows why soundness cannot replace ancestry equivalence. It is an abstract ancestry countermodel, not identical DNA distributions under a specified diploid inheritance law. The same source also composes the previously indexed finite-gARG opposite-completion theorem with elementary observation-fibre recovery to show that arbitrary deterministic coarsening cannot remove that existing ambiguity. This is credited reuse of CB-GENOME-001, not another newly counted obstruction. The graphs, owners and candidate are mathematical inputs. A finite sampled ARG cannot be onto an infinite organism history. An R path after coordinate erasure can switch loci and need not represent one DNA segment. No owner inference, biological validity, observation likelihood, effective decision procedure or empirical species assignment follows.

claims.title: Certify a leading class set without calculating every class

plain_language.question: When can we certify that chosen classes outrank every omitted class, including ones not yet seen?

Strict top-k means m(b)<m(a) for every a in T and b outside T; internal selected ranks are not asserted. A threshold implementation requires a genuine common lower bound on all selected lower endpoints and a common upper bound on all discovered outsider upper endpoints. All-class empirical error <=r plus empirical zero on undiscovered classes supplies intervals empirical±r and unseen cap r. If those premises hold simultaneously at every natural time for one fixed mass function, every successful finite data-selected-time certificate is sound; the all-time event and its probability are NOT proved. A verified all-class discrepancy eta between target and actual mass widens lower/upper/unseen bounds to l−eta, h+eta, u+eta. Given discovery, all-class empirical error, each selected true mass >3r and every selected-to-omitted true gap >4r are sufficient for certificate success, not a termination theorem. Separately, for a finite structure ensemble S, one actual classifier, exact nonnegative weights w and common partition Z=sum_S w>0, selected class partitions plus outside partition equal Z; every omitted class mass is at most rho=outside/Z=1−sum_selected p. If rho is strictly below EVERY selected p and |T|=k, T is a strict top-k set. Zero weights are allowed. These are sufficient tests, not necessary characterizations. k=0 has the literal vacuous empty-set conclusion; ties inside T are allowed, but no cross-boundary tie is certified.
